1.
 
 This memo gives guidance on the changes to the underlying entitlement conditions for 
Widowed Parent’s Allowance due to the introduction of The Bereavement Benefits (Remedial) 
Order 2023
1
 (
See Memo DMG 2-23
).
 
 These changes apply to surviving spouses and civil partners 
as well as surviving cohabiting partners.

2.
 
 The Bereavement Benefits (Remedial) Order 2023 came into force on 9.2.23.
 
 
The Remedial 
Order extends eligibility for WPA to surviving cohabiting partners with dependent children, who 
were not in a legal union with their deceased cohabiting partner on the date of their death.

3.
 
 Before the introduction of the Remedial Order, surviving partners (who were married or in a civil
  
partnership with the deceased) in receipt of WPA that entered a cohabiting partnership would 
have
 
 
 
 
 
 their payments suspended however they would retain underlying entitlement to WPA. If 
their
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 subsequent cohabiting partnership ended, as long as they continue to satisfy the 
qualifying
 
 
 
 
 
 conditions, WPA would be payable to them again (
See DMG 63037
).

CHANGE TO UNDERLYING ENTITLEMENT TO WPA WHEN ENTERING A 
COHABITING PARTNERSHIP ON OF AFTER 9.2.23
enters a cohabiting partnership with another person on or after 9.2.23.

Note 1: 
A surviving spouse or civil partner who entered a cohabiting partnership before 9.2.23 
retains underlying entitlement to WPA as long as they satisfy the qualifying conditions
2
.
1 SS CB Act 92, s 39A(4),(4A)&(4B) 2 Bereavement Benefits (Remedial) Order 2023 art 2(1)&(2)
